title: Support Swarmlet: autoresolve orchestration and safety mesh for admin utilities
creator: Claire Nguyen
description: Build a lightweight orchestration layer ("Support Swarmlet") that can run admin utilities as self-contained tasklets with automatic resolution heuristics and an enforced safety mesh. The feature combines structured runbook-as-task execution, credentialed dry-runs, telemetry-led autoresolve suggestions, and a policy circuit-breaker to prevent unsafe automated remediations. This ticket covers design, implementation, end-to-end tests, and a canary rollout path for critical firstline support flows.
rationale: On-call and first-line engineers repeatedly perform the same safe remediation steps across incidents. Automating low-risk, high-frequency fixes reduces MTTR and cognitive load while preserving safety for higher-risk ops. Existing runbook tooling is manual and inconsistent; the swarmlet aims to standardize execution, telemetry, and recovery semantics.
scope: Implement the swarmlet orchestrator, a tasklet manifest schema, a credentialed dry-run mode, automatic post-run rollbacks for failures, and a safety mesh with RBAC and circuit-breakers. Instrument token-level telemetry and evaluation hooks to detect regressions. Provide a Console page for status and rollback controls.
out_of_scope: Large-scale migration of all legacy runbooks, full enterprise policy engine integration, and Dedicated/Private deployment packaging (handled in follow-ups).
success_metrics: Reduction in median time-to-first-fix for tagged low-risk incidents by 35% within 8 weeks of rollout; fewer than 0.1% automated actions requiring manual undo; automated-run adoption of >=30% for selected playbooks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal-only alpha for SREs and support squad (dry-run only) for 2 weeks. Phase 2: gated canary with credentialed live mode for 10 selected playbooks and safety limits. Phase 3: broader enablement with RBAC gating and console controls. Each phase includes telemetry validation and a 48-hour roll-back window.
risks_mitigation: 1) Unsafe automation: enforce RBAC, preflight policy checks, and circuit-breaker thresholds. 2) Credential misuse: ephemeral credential tokens and audit logging with KMS integration. 3) Regressions: telemetry baselines and automatic rollback on error or quality drop.
notes_on_implementation:
- Orchestrator written as a small Go service with a typed manifest for tasklets.
- Tasklet runtime executes sandboxed steps and supports a dry-run mode that simulates side effects.
- Use existing admin-runbook DSL where possible but introduce a thin compatibility shim.
- Telemetry emitted via the ops-telemetry pipeline with custom tags for tasklet_id, outcome, latency, and revert_count.
telemetry_requirements: Emit metrics: tasklet.invocations, tasklet.success_rate, tasklet.autoresolve_rate, tasklet.rollback_count. Traces for each step with links to console run details. Create a dashboard tile and an alert if automated-success-rate drops >10% vs baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Alpha dry-run shows correct harmless side-effect simulation for 10 sample playbooks
Credentialed dry-run can be converted to live execution with single button and RBAC verification
Circuit-breaker halts automated execution when rollback_count > 3 in a 1h window
Telemetry dashboard shows invocation and rollback metrics; alerts firing validated
End-to-end test harness exercises canary flow and demonstrates rollback semantics
tasks: Design manifest schema and compatibility shim
Implement orchestrator service and sandboxed executor
Add credentialed dry-run API and ephemeral token flow
Wire telemetry and build dashboard tile
Create end-to-end test harness and chaos scenarios
Console UI: tasklet status, run history, and manual rollback controls
Run alpha with SRE/support and iterate on heuristics
